items.title: Submit signed code of conduct and emergency contact form
items.quote:
Please send us the signed code of conduct and your emergency contact form by
05/06/2026; we cannot confirm your room until we have both.
items.computation: The letter gives the deadline as a fixed calendar date '05/06/2026' rather than a period to be counted, so no delivery-fiction or BGB period rules apply. However, the letter is written in English for an international audience by a German organisation; the date format is ambiguous between the German/European convention (DD/MM/YYYY = 5 June 2026) and the US convention (MM/DD/YYYY = 6 May 2026), which an English-speaking recipient might also use. The document date printed elsewhere ('03/03/2026') does not resolve the ambiguity since day and month are identical. Following the rule to use the earliest plausible reading when a date is ambiguous, I take 6 May 2026 (MM/DD reading) as the due date. 6 May 2026 is a Wednesday, not a weekend or NW public holiday, so no adjustment would be needed under either reading anyway.
